evidence: Clear package/module structure with 18 packages organized by concern (context, exception, http, json, model, security, util)
High cohesion within modules: each package has focused responsibilities (e.g., context for session management, http for API communication, json for serialization)
Low coupling: average fan-out of ~2 indicates minimal interdependencies between modules
No evidence of service boundaries, network calls between internal components, or distributed deployment
Model layer is well-organized with core interfaces (BunqModel, AnchorObjectInterface) and generated endpoint/object submodules
Consistent use of dependency inversion (e.g., JsonAdapter pattern, interface-based model design)
Directory depth of 5 suggests hierarchical organization without excessive nesting typical of microservices
Tests follow the same modular structure as source code, indicating integrated but well-separated concerns
risks: Potential for tight coupling between modules if dependencies are not carefully managed
Risk of monolith becoming too large as features grow
Limited scalability options compared to microservices
